title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Citrix NetScaler zero-days exploited for weeks before disclosure, CISA warns
items.content_text: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, are being exploited worldwide. New reporting from Tenable and other researchers indicates attackers had been inside vulnerable appliances for weeks before the public disclosure, not days. The unauthenticated flaw lets an attacker run commands on a default configuration; the second is a memory-overflow bug reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the default on virtual VPN servers. Investigators found a uniquely generated webshell on each compromised device along with commands used to erase logs, and assess the activity as likely nation-state espionage. The Dutch NCSC and CISA both confirmed exploitation and added the flaws to KEV with a 30 September deadline. NetScaler commonly fronts remote-access paths into OT environments, making every unpatched appliance a live foothold.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Citrix security bulletin CTX697096; CISA KEV catalog and 27 Sep alert (30 Sep deadline); Dutch NCSC; Tenable and Rapid7 research; reported by Help Net Security, BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Exploited for weeks before disclosure; Citrix confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026; added to CISA KEV 27 Sep 2026 (federal deadline 30 Sep 2026)

items.title: Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
items.content_text: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote alarms and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It remains the only confirmed case of OT tampering in this edition, with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure.

items.title: A third vessel’s hijacked-valve claim stays unverified as a Texas regulator urges operators to harden defenses
items.content_text: The Coast Guard and FBI boarded the tanker VL Prosperity off Galveston on 21 August and a second US-bound tanker on 24 August, with Rear Admiral Amy Grable confirming investigators found evidence of a malicious cyber actor on the vessels’ IT and other onboard systems; neither ship was found unsafe to operate, and the Coast Guard has not publicly attributed the intrusions to Iran despite Iranian state media claiming credit. A third vessel, the LNG carrier Vivit Africa, reported a suspected cyberattack near the Strait of Gibraltar in September; its crew alleged attackers briefly took control of tank-pressure and relief-valve systems, but the Italian Coast Guard and Korean Register have confirmed only a systems malfunction, not a cyberattack. On 24 September, Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a public statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to strengthen their cyber defenses.
tags: Incident — Coast Guard- and FBI-confirmed cyber intrusions on two Galveston-bound tankers boarded in August; a third vessel’s (LNG carrier) crew claim of a hijacked safety system unverified by any maritime authority; a Texas regulator cites the boardings in a public statement; no confirmed shore-side disruption

items.title: A cyber incident stopped container handling at Tanjung Pelepas — the restart began with manual gate-ins
items.content_text: A cyber incident detected on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas, one of the world’s largest transhipment hubs, to suspend container terminal operations and its terminal operating systems as a precaution. A phased restart beginning the next day initially relied on manual processing for export container gate-ins, and by 15 September the port said normal operations had resumed with system recovery ongoing. For OT defenders it’s a clean illustration of the pattern that actually causes industrial downtime: nothing reported suggests crane or equipment controls were touched — losing the system that decides where each container goes was enough to stop the boxes moving.
tags: Incident — confirmed cyber incident; container terminal operations and terminal operating systems suspended at a major transhipment hub; phased manual restart; ransomware not confirmed by the operator

items.title: Chained flaws in an IO-Link master hand an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor data
items.content_text: CERT@VDE disclosed 18 vulnerabilities in Pepperl+Fuchs’s ICE2 and ICE3 series IO-Link masters on 16 September in advisory VDE-2026-014. The worst, CVE-2026-27546, is an authentication bypass scored CVSS 9.8; a companion flaw, CVE-2026-27565, lets an attacker inject operating-system commands through a malicious IODD file upload that persists after reboot. Chained together, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover.
tags: Research — CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014: 18 CVEs across Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3 IO-Link masters, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass and a persistent command-injection flaw; chainable for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation

items.title: One unauthenticated packet can crash the time-series database behind industrial telemetry
items.content_text: Ridge Security disclosed CVE-2026-42542 on 23 September, a pre-authentication integer underflow in TDengine’s RPC protocol handler that lets a single crafted packet crash the taosd service with no login required. TDengine is an open-source time-series database widely used to store sensor and telemetry data from industrial and IoT deployments; the flaw affects versions 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5 and is fixed in 3.4.1.6. Ridge Security says it has seen no exploitation in the wild and isn’t aware of public exploit code, but the flaw needs no credentials and no user interaction — only network reach to port 6030 — making it a low-effort way to knock out the historian or telemetry store behind a monitoring dashboard.
tags: Research — Ridge Security discloses CVE-2026-42542 (CVSS 7.5), TDengine 3.4.0.0–3.4.1.5; unauthenticated integer underflow crashes the taosd service with a single packet; fixed version available; no known exploitation

_otthreatfeed.category: Research — Ridge Security discloses CVE-2026-42542 (CVSS 7.5), TDengine 3.4.0.0–3.4.1.5; unauthenticated integer underflow crashes the taosd service with a single packet; fixed version available; no known exploitation

items.title: Forescout: only 13% of OT network segments are actually OT-only
items.content_text: Forescout examined 47,700 network segments holding more than 2.5 million devices across 209 organizations, publishing findings on 22 September. Just 13% of segments containing OT devices were dedicated exclusively to OT, and only 6% of medical-device segments were isolated solely for that equipment; the average segment held 54 devices across four device categories. The researchers conclude that OT and medical devices routinely share network space with general enterprise assets, widening the blast radius available to an attacker who lands anywhere on a converged network — a structural exposure rather than an active campaign.
tags: Research — Forescout analysis of 47,700 network segments across 209 organizations; only 13% of OT-containing segments are dedicated exclusively to OT (6% for medical-only segments); sector-aggregated statistics, not a specific incident; no CVE

items.title: A second MikroTik RouterOS flaw joins CISA’s exploited list as the “MikroTrick” chain keeps hitting the OT remote-access edge
items.content_text: CISA added a second MikroTik RouterOS flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog around 25 September, joining CVE-2026-86060, added 10 September. Together they form the “MikroTrick” chain: CERT Polska and independent researchers have tracked in-the-wild exploitation since at least early September, with attack logs dating to before MikroTik shipped its fix, giving an unauthenticated attacker full administrative console access. Trackers disagree on the second CVE’s exact number — CERT Polska’s technical analysis identifies it as CVE-2026-67279, while some vendor write-ups and trackers list CVE-2026-67277 — but agree it pairs with CVE-2026-86060 in the same exploit chain. These routers commonly front remote-access and cellular-telemetry links into field sites and small, unattended facilities that rarely get timely firmware updates.
tags: Advisory — “MikroTrick” SSH-bypass chain in MikroTik RouterOS gives unauthenticated administrative access; CVE-2026-86060 added to CISA KEV 10 Sep, a second RouterOS CVE added around 25 Sep (trackers differ on whether it is CVE-2026-67279 or CVE-2026-67277); confirmed active exploitation since early September; fixed firmware available

_otthreatfeed.category: Advisory — “MikroTrick” SSH-bypass chain in MikroTik RouterOS gives unauthenticated administrative access; CVE-2026-86060 added to CISA KEV 10 Sep, a second RouterOS CVE added around 25 Sep (trackers differ on whether it is CVE-2026-67279 or CVE-2026-67277); confirmed active exploitation since early September; fixed firmware available
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog; CERT Polska advisory and technical analysis; reported by The Hacker News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Exploitation tracked from early Sep 2026; CVE-2026-86060 added to KEV 10 Sep (deadline 13 Sep); second RouterOS CVE added around 25 Sep 2026

items.title: Check Point’s federal patch deadline has passed for two exploited flaws spanning the VPN gateway and the server that manages it
items.content_text: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two separate flaws now past their federal remediation deadline. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation issue on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal affecting Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September alongside flaws in Arista VeloCloud and F5 BIG-IP APM; the 25 September deadline has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small, unmanned sites.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway/Spark VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers/SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed

items.title: Nearly a thousand small Zyxel switches were compromised through a flaw patched back in June
items.content_text: GreyNoise reported on 22 September that 996 Zyxel GS1900 managed switches across 48 countries had been compromised through CVE-2026-7273, a stack-based buffer overflow in the switches’ CGI web interface that lets an unauthenticated attacker on the local network run operating-system commands. Zyxel released a fix for it in June; CISA added the CVE to KEV with a 24 September deadline that has now passed. The attacker, described only as Chinese-speaking, extracted device configurations, networking details and hashed root credentials using heavily obfuscated Python exploit code; 564 of the compromised switches still had factory-default credentials. Small managed switches like the GS1900 are common in plant and utility networks, where firmware updates often lag.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-7273, Zyxel GS1900 managed switches; stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI web interface; 996 switches across 48 countries reported compromised; added to CISA KEV with a 24 Sep 2026 deadline, now passed; fix available since June

items.title: A broken authentication check in Schneider’s flagship M580 safety PLC needs a validated patch window
items.content_text: Schneider Electric disclosed CVE-2026-3869 on 9 September in advisory SEVD-2026-251-04: an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm affecting Modicon M580 controllers below application level 4.00, M580 Safety below 4.20, and Modicon MC80 units. The flaw scores CVSS v4 9.2 and could let an attacker who reaches the controller bypass authentication on management functions. The M580 is Schneider’s flagship PLC platform, deployed widely across process manufacturing, water, oil and gas and power applications, and the Safety variant runs safety-instrumented functions tied directly to process protection. No exploitation has been reported, and fixed firmware is available, but like most safety-certified controllers it can’t be patched without a validated change-control cycle, so unpatched units are likely to stay in service for weeks or months — making network isolation the interim control that matters most.
tags: Advisory — CVE-2026-3869 (CVSS v4 9.2), Schneider Electric Modicon M580, M580 Safety and MC80 PLCs; incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm; fixed firmware available (SEVD-2026-251-04), no known exploitation

items.title: FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
items.content_text: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk on 24 September, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. The agencies say intruders searched the company’s systems for terms like “customers” and “SCADA” and staged customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; downstream customers referenced in the guidance include power utilities and transportation entities. The guidance recommends least-privilege integrator access, on-demand and auditable remote sessions, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security terms in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if an integrator is compromised.
tags: Guidance — FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion

items.title: NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — comments are open until 30 November
items.content_text: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail and maritime vessels; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026, and it lands the same week as the FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above).
